name: Regional kingdoms of India
summary: The many Hindu, Rajput and other regional kingdoms of India that are not shown as separate entries, from early states to the Rajput kingdoms of Rajasthan.

location.value: Across the Indian subcontinent, from Rajasthan and central India to the Deccan and the far south.
location.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

terrain.value: The Ganges plains, the Thar Desert of Rajasthan, the Aravalli hills, the Deccan plateau and the coastal plains.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

climate.value: Monsoon climate: a hot dry season, heavy summer rains and a cooler winter; desert in the north-west.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

resources.value: Fertile farmland, cotton, spices, timber, salt, iron, and gems such as diamonds from the Deccan.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

disasters.value: Famines when the monsoon failed, floods along the great rivers, and epidemics in war and drought years.
disasters.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

population.value: Not known for most kingdoms; individual states ranged from small chiefdoms to kingdoms of several million people.
population.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

urbanisation.value: Capitals and fort cities such as Chittorgarh, Ajmer, Jodhpur, Amber and Udaipur, plus temple and trading towns.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

disease.value: Malaria, cholera and smallpox were common, with epidemics after famines and during wars.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

migration.value: Clans, traders and pilgrims moved widely; Rajput clans settled in Rajasthan and central India in the early medieval period.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

economicBase.value: Farming of wheat, rice, millet and cotton, taxed by kings, along with crafts and trade in cloth and spices.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

tradeRoutes.value: Overland routes across north India and the Deccan, and sea trade from western and eastern ports to Arabia and South-East Asia.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

wealth.value: No estimate; wealth came from land revenue, trade tolls and temple endowments, and varied greatly between kingdoms.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

moneyAndTax.value: Kings minted gold, silver and copper coins and took a share of the harvest as land revenue, plus trade tolls.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

inequality.value: A hierarchy of castes, with kings, warrior clans and priests at the top and landless labourers at the bottom.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

governmentType.value: Hereditary monarchies ruled by rajas or ranas, often supported by clan lords who held land in return for service.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

keyRulers.value: Prithviraj Chauhan. Rana Sanga. Maharana Pratap.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

succession.value: Usually hereditary, often to the eldest son, but disputed successions between brothers and clans were common.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

institutions.value: Royal courts with ministers, land grants to temples and Brahmins, and clan lords who served the king in war.
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

stability.value: Uneven: wars between neighbouring kingdoms were frequent, and many states were short-lived.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

eliteConflict.value: Rivalries between Rajput clans and between royal brothers often weakened kingdoms against outside rivals.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

armyAndTech.value: Armies of horsemen, war elephants and foot soldiers, defended by hill forts such as Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

majorWars.value: Wars with each other and with the sultanates and Mughals.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

territoryChange.value: Kingdoms rose and fell over two thousand years.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

alliancesRivals.value: Shifting alliances between kingdoms and with the Delhi Sultanate, the Mughals, the Marathas and later the British.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

inventions.value: Not specific to these kingdoms, which shared wider Indian advances in mathematics, metalwork and textiles.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

scienceEducation.value: Sanskrit learning in temples and courts, including astronomy, grammar and medicine; Jain and Buddhist scholars too.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

openness.value: Varied by kingdom; many welcomed traders and religious teachers, and some made alliances with outside powers.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

communicationTransport.value: Roads for ox carts and caravans, river boats, and messengers on horseback between courts and forts.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

religion.value: Mostly Hinduism, with Jainism (strong among merchants in Rajasthan and Gujarat) and Buddhism in earlier centuries.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

languageWriting.value: Sanskrit for religion and courts, and regional languages such as Rajasthani, Hindi, Marathi, Telugu and Tamil.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

artsArchitecture.value: Hindu and Jain temples such as the Dilwara temples at Mount Abu, hill forts, palaces, and Rajput miniature painting.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

socialStructure.value: A caste society: kings and warrior clans, Brahmin priests, merchants, farmers and artisans, with outcaste groups at the bottom.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

sharedIdentity.value: Shared Hindu, Jain and Rajput traditions.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

dailyLife.value: Brick and stone houses; wheat, rice, lentils.
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

neighbours.value: Each other, the Delhi Sultanate, the Mughal Empire, the Marathas and finally the British East India Company.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

ideasReligions.value: Hindu traditions, including devotional (bhakti) movements, and Jain teachings that shaped trade and temple building.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

colonisation.value: By 1818 most surviving kingdoms, including the Rajput states, had signed treaties making them British princely states.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

riseSignals.value: Varied: new kingdoms often rose when larger empires weakened, as Rajput states did after the decline of the Gurjara-Pratiharas.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

peakPeriod.value: Varied by kingdom; for example, Mewar was strong under Rana Kumbha and Rana Sanga in the 1400s and early 1500s.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

declineSignals.value: Conquest by the sultanates, the Mughals or the British.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

outcome.value: Absorbed by larger empires or the British.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

sources.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs

overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Middle kingdoms of India; Wikipedia: Rajputs
